title: B-semiampleness for compact log-smooth Kähler fibrations
main_claim: For f:Y→X a connected-fiber map of compact Kähler manifolds with effective SNC Δ (coefficients in [0,1]) and K_Y+Δ ~_Q f^*L, the moduli b-line bundle defined by lc thresholds is b-semiample. That is: on some compact Kähler model S, M_{S1}=ν^*M_S holds for every higher smooth model, and a multiple of M_S is globally generated.
coverage:
I read all 9 sections in full and checked these steps:
- Sec 2: threshold lemma and the degenerate cases.
- Sec 3: root eigenline. Uniqueness of the χ-eigenform, the residue spectral sequence putting F^d in weight d+k, the residue identification, and invariance under change of model.
- Sec 4: the exact Hodge order formula ord = min_E (l_E+1−a_E)/a_E. I checked the change of variables dt = N u^{N-1} du, the extension test for α_E ≥ 0, the failure test via the shifted order e(α_E + a_E/N), and the exactness argument. Also the trace identity t_P − 1 with its sign, the multivariable extension by Laurent coefficients plus Hartogs, b-descent with l_E = −δ_E + a_E c_P, and the residue norm.
- Sec 5: marked klt family, fiber splitting, realizing finite étale covers via the semidirect product, constructibility of images, the Douady/Hilbert parameter spaces with a Baire domination argument, and the product volume and norm formula.
- Sec 6: projective comparison via BFMT, with arbitrary vertical coefficients.
- Sec 7: the rationalization trick. With J = B^{-1}B' and C = J^{1/2}, I verified J^tB = BJ, C^tBC = B', and the transfer of the Hodge–Riemann relations. Also the full H^2 polarization of signature (2, h^{1,1}), neat level giving unipotence, Baily–Borel and Borel extension, λ ≅ det E ⊗ ℓ^2 with det E trivial at neat level, and generators carried to generators under cup product (by the splitting argument).
- Sec 8: unit extension from two-sided log bounds, and descent through Stein factorization with the finite-norm construction.
Not checked against the sources: MWWWZ25 Cor 1.3, BFMT25 Thms 1.5/5.2/5.5/6.28, FF25 Thm 1.1, and Toma/Fujiki Douady compactness.

issues.description: The whole product-decomposition step depends on MWWWZ25 version 1 Corollary 1.3. The paper uses it to give, for a compact Kähler klt pair with K+D numerically trivial, a finite étale cover that splits as a product with the boundary carried entirely by a rationally connected (hence projective) factor. I did not check this hypothesis/conclusion match against the cited preprint (in particular boundary support and the smoothness of the factors).
issues.evidence: The proof says 'the decomposition theorem of Matsumura--Wang--Wu--Zhang applies to this smooth effective klt pair [version 1, Corollary 1.3]' and then states 'The boundary is entirely on Q' without arguing it.

issues.description: The projective factor and the period factors rest on BFMT25: Thm 1.5 with Def 6.18, Thm 6.28 identifying the Hodge and threshold moduli parts, and Thms 5.2/5.5 for the Baily–Borel extension with Schmid-extension pullback. The hypotheses were restated in the paper but not checked against the source. The Baily–Borel extension step is essentially Borel's extension theorem at neat level, so it is low risk.
issues.evidence: 'It follows from Theorem~1.5 of [BFMT25]... Theorem~6.28 of [BFMT25]'; 'We use the following precise consequence of [Theorems~5.2 and~5.5]{BFMT25}'.

sibling_notes: The four family-033 siblings already on the board (Iitaka subadditivity / log Kodaira papers) all returned no_gap_found. None of them shares a lemma with this paper, so there is no circularity: this paper uses only external citations (BFMT25, FF25, MWWWZ25), not companion OAI preprints.
